## My Reasoning

I have farmed this land in Quzhou my whole life. My father farmed it before me. In this county, everyone grows winter wheat and summer corn — that is what the soil and the seasons call for, and I see no reason to change what has worked for fifty years.

I have about 10 mu of land. My sons have moved to the city, so I work it mostly alone, though I hire the village machine operator for ploughing, seeding, and harvest. My knees can no longer handle deep hand-labour, so I pay for mechanized services. This costs money but I cannot avoid it at my age.

For **winter wheat**, I will plant all 10 mu starting in early October. I have been using the Jimai 22 variety for over a decade — it is reliable against cold and rust. The seed station sells it every year. I apply compound fertilizer as base fertilizer when I plough, then top-dress urea at jointing. I irrigate three times: before winter sets in, at jointing, and at heading. Skipping the heading irrigation risks empty grains and I will not do that. I spray once for weeds in winter, and once for aphids and powdery mildew in spring.

For **summer maize**, I plant right after wheat harvest in mid-June — I cannot waste days because the season is short. I use Xianyu 335 hybrid seed, which the township agricultural station has pushed for years and yields well. I do rotary tillage quickly to prepare the seedbed. I apply fertilizer in two splits. Summer rain usually helps, but I irrigate once at tasseling if it is dry. I spray for corn borer once. By late September, the combine comes and I am done.

I do not grow vegetables or other crops. At 72, I keep things simple. I know these two crops. I know their timing. I do not experiment.
